name: Access to Electricity
definition: The percentage of the country's population with access to an electricity supply, whether from the grid or from off-grid systems. Use the latest official national figure for the report's fiscal year, sourced from the national statistics office, the most recent census, or the national energy department. Feeds the Access to Electricity KPI. Note that the valid range is 0 to 1, so enter the value as a decimal proportion (for example 0.95 for 95%), and report the national figure rather than coverage within the utility's service area.

name: Air Connectivity per 1000 People
definition: The country's air connectivity expressed per 1,000 persons of national population, indicating how well connected the country is by scheduled air services relative to its population size. Derive it from the national air connectivity measure (see IATA Air Connectivity Score) and the latest official national population figure for the report's fiscal year. Feeds the Air Connectivity per 1000 People KPI. Ensure the same population vintage is used here as in the Population input so context indicators remain consistent.
synonyms: air transport connectivity per thousand people

name: Air Connectivity per Unit GDP
definition: The country's air connectivity expressed per unit of gross domestic product (% per unit GDP), indicating how well connected the country is by scheduled air services relative to the size of its economy. Derive it from the national air connectivity measure and the latest official GDP figure published by the national statistics office or central bank for the report's fiscal year. Feeds the Air Connectivity per Unit GDP KPI. Take care to use the same GDP vintage as other GDP-based context inputs.
synonyms: air transport connectivity per unit of economic output

name: Average Household Size
definition: The average number of persons per household across the country, expressed in persons per household. Source the latest official figure from the national statistics office or the most recent national census; where no direct figure is published it is the national population divided by the number of households. Feeds the Average Household Size KPI. Use the national figure, not an estimate for the utility's service area only.

name: Fuel Pricing Regulation
definition: A descriptive selection identifying how fuel prices are regulated in the country, chosen from the managed list of options provided in PRISM. Select the option that best describes the current national arrangement for setting or controlling the price of fuel (for example regulated by a national authority or set by the market), as at the end of the report's fiscal year. Feeds the Fuel Pricing Regulation KPI. This describes the national fuel-price regime, not the utility's own fuel purchase contracts.

name: Fuel Supply Access
definition: A descriptive selection identifying the country's access to fuel supply, chosen from the managed list of options provided in PRISM. Select the option that best describes how the country obtains its fuel (for example direct import, regional distribution hub, or domestic supply) as at the end of the report's fiscal year. Feeds the Fuel Supply Access KPI. This is a country-level characteristic, not a description of the utility's individual supply contracts.

name: GDP Per Capita
definition: The country's gross domestic product divided by its population, expressed in currency per person. Use the latest official figure for the report's fiscal year from the national statistics office, central bank, or ministry of finance national accounts. Feeds the GDP per Capita KPI. Enter the value in the utility's local currency; PRISM converts to USD using the USD Exchange Rate input, so do not pre-convert.

name: Households
definition: The total number of households in the country, expressed as a count of households. Use the latest official national figure from the national statistics office or the most recent census, updated to the report's fiscal year where an official projection is available. Feeds the Households KPI. Report the national total, not the number of households in the utility's service area and not the utility's customer count, which can differ substantially.

name: IATA Air Connectivity Score
definition: The country's air connectivity score as published by the International Air Transport Association (IATA), expressed as a percentage. Use the most recent IATA score available for the report's fiscal year; where the national statistics office or civil aviation authority republishes the figure, confirm it matches the IATA source. Feeds the IATA Air Connectivity Score KPI. Do not substitute a locally derived connectivity measure for the IATA-published score.

name: Inflation Rate
definition: The country's annual rate of consumer price inflation for the reporting year, expressed as a percentage. Use the latest official figure from the national statistics office or central bank for the report's fiscal year; deflation is entered as a negative value. Feeds the Inflation Rate KPI. Take care to match the utility's fiscal year rather than defaulting to the calendar-year figure where the two differ.

name: Islands
definition: The total number of islands making up the country, expressed as a count of islands. Use the official figure published by the national statistics office or national mapping authority, including uninhabited islands where that is the basis of the official count. Feeds the Islands KPI. Record the national total, not only the islands served by the utility.

name: Land Area
definition: The total land area of the country, expressed in square kilometres (km2). Use the latest official figure from the national statistics office or national mapping authority, covering land area only and excluding territorial waters and exclusive economic zone. Feeds the Land Area KPI. A common error is reporting the EEZ or total maritime area, which for Pacific island countries is vastly larger than the land area.

name: Population
definition: The total resident population of the country, expressed in persons. Use the latest official national figure from the national statistics office, based on the most recent census or the official mid-year estimate for the report's fiscal year. Feeds the Population KPI. Report the national population, not the population of the utility's service area, which may cover only some islands or urban centres.

name: Rural Population
definition: The share of the country's population living in rural areas, expressed as a percentage. Use the latest official figure from the national statistics office or the most recent census, applying the national statistical definition of rural areas for the report's fiscal year. Feeds the Rural Population KPI. Check that the rural and urban population shares entered are consistent and together account for the whole population.

name: Unemployment Rate
definition: The country's unemployment rate for the reporting year, expressed as the percentage of the labour force that is unemployed. Use the latest official figure from the national statistics office, typically from the labour force survey or census, for the report's fiscal year. Feeds the Unemployment Rate KPI. Note that survey-based rates can differ from registered-unemployment counts; use the official labour force survey definition where available.

name: Urban Population
definition: The share of the country's population living in urban areas, expressed as a percentage. Use the latest official figure from the national statistics office or the most recent census, applying the national statistical definition of urban areas for the report's fiscal year. Feeds the Urban Population KPI. Check that the urban and rural population shares entered are consistent and together account for the whole population.

name: Accounting Standards
definition: A descriptive selection identifying the accounting standards under which the utility prepares its financial statements, chosen from the managed list of options provided in PRISM. Select the standard actually applied in the utility's audited financial statements for the reporting year (for example IFRS or a national standard), as stated in the accounting policies note of the annual report. Feeds the Accounting Standards KPI. If the utility changed standards during the year, report the standard applied to the year-end financial statements.

name: Electricity Regulation
definition: A descriptive selection identifying how the utility's electricity business is regulated, chosen from the managed list of options provided in PRISM. Select the option that best describes the regulatory arrangement applying to the utility during the reporting year, for example oversight by an independent regulator, regulation by a government ministry, or self-regulation. Feeds the Electricity Regulation KPI. Report the arrangement that actually governs the utility's tariffs and service standards, not simply what legislation provides for on paper.

name: Feeder Type
definition: A descriptive selection identifying the type of feeders that characterise the utility's distribution network, chosen from the managed list of options provided in PRISM. Select the option that best describes the utility's network configuration (for example predominantly overhead, underground, or mixed) as at the end of the reporting year. Feeds the Feeder Type KPI. Where the network is mixed, choose the option representing the predominant arrangement rather than the ideal or planned configuration.

name: Power Quality Standards
definition: A descriptive selection identifying the power quality standards the utility operates to, chosen from the managed list of options provided in PRISM. Select the standard formally applied to the utility's supply voltage and frequency performance during the reporting year, whether set by legislation, the regulator, or the utility's own adopted standard. Feeds the Power Quality Standards KPI. Report the standard actually in force for the utility, not aspirational standards under consideration.

name: Power Purchase Costs
definition: The total cost incurred by the utility during the reporting year to purchase electricity from third parties, such as independent power producers (IPPs), expressed in currency. Include all amounts payable under power purchase agreements and other bulk electricity purchases for the fiscal year, and exclude the cost of fuel used in the utility's own generation. Feeds the Power Purchase Costs KPI. Enter the value in the utility's local currency for the utility's fiscal year; leave blank only if the utility purchases no power from third parties.

name: USD Exchange Rate
definition: The exchange rate between the utility's local currency and the United States dollar for the reporting year, expressed as the number of local currency units per one US dollar. Use the official rate published by the central bank or national statistics office for the utility's fiscal year, applied consistently from year to year. This rate is used to convert all local-currency financial inputs to USD for cross-utility comparison in the PPA Benchmarking Report, and feeds the USD Exchange Rate KPI. A common error is entering the rate inverted (USD per local unit) or using a spot rate inconsistent with the fiscal year being reported.
synonyms: foreign exchange rate to US dollar

name: Does the Annual Report disclose performance relative to the Strategic Plan?
definition: A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility's Annual Report discloses actual performance against the objectives and targets set in its Strategic Plan. Answer "Yes" only if the published Annual Report for the reporting year explicitly compares achieved results with the goals or targets of the adopted Strategic Plan, not merely if both documents exist separately. Feeds the Does the Annual Report disclose performance relative to the Strategic Plan KPI. General narrative about achievements without reference to the plan's targets does not qualify as a "Yes".

name: Is the Annual Report audited?
definition: A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the financial statements in the utility's Annual Report are independently audited. Answer "Yes" only if the financial statements for the reporting year have been audited by an independent external auditor, such as a registered audit firm or the national audit office, and an audit opinion has been issued. Feeds the Is the Annual Report audited KPI. An internal audit review or an audit still in progress at the time of reporting does not qualify as a "Yes".

name: Is the Annual Report completed within four months of the end of the Reporting Year?
definition: A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility's Annual Report is completed within four months of the end of the reporting year. Answer "Yes" only if the Annual Report for the reporting year was finalised, including audited financial statements, within four months of the utility's fiscal year end. Feeds the Is the Annual Report completed within four months of the end of the reporting year KPI. Measure the four months from the utility's own fiscal year end, not the calendar year end, and use the completion date rather than the date of tabling in parliament.

name: Is a Code of Conduct implemented?
definition: A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility's Code of Conduct is actively implemented, as distinct from merely existing. Answer "Yes" only if the code is applied in practice during the reporting year — for example staff are made aware of it and acknowledge it, training or induction covers it, and breaches are acted upon. Feeds the Is a Code of Conduct implemented KPI. A code that has been adopted but is not communicated or enforced should be answered "No" here even if "Is a Code of Conduct in place?" is answered "Yes".

name: Is a Code of Conduct in place?
definition: A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility has a formally adopted Code of Conduct. Answer "Yes" only if a written code of conduct or code of ethics covering directors and/or staff has been formally approved by the Board or management and was current during the reporting year. Feeds the Is a Code of Conduct in place KPI. A draft code, or general provisions scattered across HR policies without a formally adopted code, should be answered "No".

name: Is a Commercial Mandate implemented?
definition: A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility's commercial mandate is followed in practice, as distinct from merely existing in its founding documents. Answer "Yes" only if, during the reporting year, the utility actually operated on commercial principles — for example pursuing cost recovery, being managed to financial performance targets, and having non-commercial obligations identified and treated separately. Feeds the Is a Commercial mandate implemented KPI. A utility whose legislation requires commercial operation but which is run to non-commercial directives in practice should answer "No" here.

name: Is a Commercial Mandate in place?
definition: A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility has a formal commercial mandate. Answer "Yes" only if the utility's establishing legislation, charter, articles, or state-owned-enterprise framework formally requires it to operate as a commercial business, for example to be financially self-sustaining or to earn a commercial return. Feeds the Is a Commercial mandate in place KPI. This item concerns the formal mandate only; whether the mandate is actually followed is captured by the separate "Is a Commercial Mandate implemented?" item.

name: Are Ministers appointed to the Board?
definition: A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether serving government ministers are appointed as members of the utility's Board of Directors. Answer "Yes" only if one or more persons holding ministerial office sat on the Board at any time during the reporting year. Feeds the Are Ministers appointed to the Board KPI. The question concerns ministers themselves, not civil servants or ministry officials appointed as government representatives, and not ministers acting solely as shareholders.

name: Does the CEO's Performance Contract include Annual Reviews?
definition: A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the CEO's performance contract provides for annual performance reviews. Answer "Yes" only if the contract requires the Board (or responsible authority) to formally review the CEO's performance against the contract's targets at least once a year, and such a review was conducted for the reporting year. Feeds the Does the CEOs performance contract include annual reviews KPI. Informal or ad hoc discussions of performance without a documented annual review process do not qualify as a "Yes".
synonyms: yearly performance assessment of chief executive

name: Is the CEO on a Performance Contract?
definition: A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility's Chief Executive Officer is employed under a performance contract. Answer "Yes" only if the CEO's contract of employment includes defined, measurable performance targets or key performance indicators against which the CEO is assessed. Feeds the Is the CEO on a performance contract KPI. A standard employment contract without explicit performance targets should be answered "No".

name: Does the Strategic Plan include three or more years of forecasts?
definition: A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility's Strategic Plan includes forecasts covering three or more years. Answer "Yes" only if the adopted Strategic Plan contains financial and/or operational forecasts (for example demand, revenue, expenditure, or investment projections) spanning at least three future years. Feeds the Does the Strategic Plan include three or more years of forecasts KPI. A plan stating multi-year objectives but containing only a single-year budget or no quantified forecasts should be answered "No".

name: Has a Strategic Plan been adopted?
definition: A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility has formally adopted a Strategic Plan. Answer "Yes" only if a written strategic (or corporate) plan setting out the utility's objectives and direction has been formally approved by the Board and was current during the reporting year. Feeds the Has a Strategic Plan been adopted KPI. A plan that is in draft, expired, or awaiting Board approval should be answered "No".

name: Is the Strategic Plan implemented?
definition: A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility's Strategic Plan is actively implemented, as distinct from merely being adopted. Answer "Yes" only if, during the reporting year, the plan genuinely guided operations — for example its initiatives were resourced and under way, and progress against it was monitored and reported to the Board or management. Feeds the Is the Strategic Plan implemented KPI. A plan that sits on the shelf without linked actions, budgets, or progress reporting should be answered "No" even if formally adopted.

name: FTE Employees in Distribution
definition: The number of full-time equivalent (FTE) employees engaged in the utility's distribution function for the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll, converted to full-time equivalents (two half-time staff = 1 FTE); exclude contractors and consultants. Feeds the Customers per Distribution Employee KPI. Report FTE, not headcount — a part-time employee counts as a fraction of an FTE.

name: FTE Employees in Generation
definition: The number of full-time equivalent (FTE) employees engaged in the utility's generation function for the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll, converted to full-time equivalents (two half-time staff = 1 FTE); exclude contractors and consultants. Feeds the Generation Labor Productivity KPI. Staff who split their time across functions should be apportioned so that each person's FTE is counted only once across divisions.

name: FTE Employees in Transmission
definition: The number of full-time equivalent (FTE) employees engaged in the utility's transmission function for the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll, converted to full-time equivalents (two half-time staff = 1 FTE); exclude contractors and consultants. Utilities that do not operate a separate transmission network should leave this blank rather than repeating distribution staff here.

name: Administrative Employees Female
definition: The number of female employees working in the utility's administrative division, reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the Administrative Employees Female %, Administrative Employees Total, Total Employees Female and IPP Generation KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure — count each person once regardless of hours worked.

name: Administrative Employees Male
definition: The number of male employees working in the utility's administrative division, reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the Administrative Employees Male %, Administrative Employees Total and Total Employees Male KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure — count each person once regardless of hours worked.

name: Administrative Employees Total
definition: The total number of employees in the utility's administrative division, in employees. It is calculated automatically as the sum of the reported male and female administrative employee counts, so no separate entry is required. Feeds the Administrative Employees Female % and Administrative Employees Male % KPIs. If the total looks wrong, correct the underlying male and female counts rather than this value.

name: Employees Female
definition: The total number of female employees across the whole utility, in employees. It is calculated by summing the female headcounts reported for each division (executive, technical, finance, procurement, human resources, PR/marketing/customer service, administrative, ICT and other), so no separate entry is required. Feeds the Employees Female % and Total Employees KPIs, which underpin the PPA's utility-wide gender-representation reporting. Ensure each employee is assigned to exactly one division so this total does not double-count anyone.

name: Employees Male
definition: The total number of male employees across the whole utility, in employees. It is calculated by summing the male headcounts reported for each division (executive, technical, finance, procurement, human resources, PR/marketing/customer service, administrative, ICT and other), so no separate entry is required. Feeds the Employees Male % and Total Employees KPIs, which underpin the PPA's utility-wide gender-representation reporting. Ensure each employee is assigned to exactly one division so this total does not double-count anyone.

name: Executive Employees Female
definition: The number of female employees in the utility's executive division (the senior leadership team), reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants, board members who are not employees, and vacant positions. Feeds the Executive Employees Female %, Executive Employees Total and Total Employees Female KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

name: Executive Employees Male
definition: The number of male employees in the utility's executive division (the senior leadership team), reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants, board members who are not employees, and vacant positions. Feeds the Executive Employees Male %, Executive Employees Total and Total Employees Male KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

name: Executive Employees Total
definition: The total number of employees in the utility's executive division (the senior leadership team), in employees. It is calculated automatically as the sum of the reported male and female executive employee counts, so no separate entry is required. Feeds the Executive Employees Female % and Executive Employees Male % KPIs. If the total looks wrong, correct the underlying male and female counts rather than this value.

name: Finance Employees Female
definition: The number of female employees in the utility's finance division, reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the Finance Employees Female %, Finance Employees Total and Total Employees Female KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

name: Finance Employees Male
definition: The number of male employees in the utility's finance division, reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the Finance Employees Female %, Finance Employees Male %, Finance Employees Total and Total Employees Male KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

name: Finance Employees Total
definition: The total number of employees in the utility's finance division, in employees. It is calculated automatically as the sum of the reported male and female finance employee counts, so no separate entry is required. Feeds the Finance Employees Female % and Finance Employees Male % KPIs. If the total looks wrong, correct the underlying male and female counts rather than this value.

name: Gender of 2IC
definition: Records the gender of the utility's second-in-command — typically the Deputy CEO, Chief Operating Officer or most senior executive reporting directly to the CEO — as at the end of the reporting year; this is a gender value, not a number. Report the person actually occupying the role at year end, including an acting incumbent if the position is filled in an acting capacity. Feeds the Gender of Utility 2nd in command KPI, part of the PPA's reporting of gender representation in utility leadership.

name: Gender of CEO
definition: Records the gender of the utility's Chief Executive Officer (or equivalent most senior executive, such as a General Manager) as at the end of the reporting year; this is a gender value, not a number. Report the person actually occupying the role at year end, including an acting CEO if the position is filled in an acting capacity. Feeds the Gender of Utility CEO KPI, part of the PPA's reporting of gender representation in utility leadership.

name: Human Resource Employees Female
definition: The number of female employees in the utility's human resources division, reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the HR Employees Female %, HR Employees Total and Total Employees Female KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

name: Human Resource Employees Male
definition: The number of male employees in the utility's human resources division, reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the HR Employees Male % and HR Employees Total KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

name: Human Resource Employees Total
definition: The total number of employees in the utility's human resources division, in employees. It is calculated as the sum of the reported male and female human resources employee counts, so no separate entry is required. Feeds the HR Employees Female % and HR Employees Male % KPIs. If the total looks wrong, correct the underlying male and female counts rather than this value.

name: ICT Employees Female
definition: The number of female employees in the utility's ICT (information and communication technology) division, reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the ICT Employees Female %, ICT Employees Total and Total Employees Female KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

name: ICT Employees Male
definition: The number of male employees in the utility's ICT (information and communication technology) division, reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the ICT Employees Male %, ICT Employees Total and Total Employees Male KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

name: ICT Employees Total
definition: The total number of employees in the utility's ICT (information and communication technology) division, in employees. It is calculated as the sum of the reported male and female ICT employee counts, so no separate entry is required. Feeds the ICT Employees Female % and ICT Employees Male % KPIs. If the total looks wrong, correct the underlying male and female counts rather than this value.

name: Other Employees Female
definition: The number of female employees in divisions not covered by the named categories (executive, technical, finance, procurement, human resources, PR/marketing/customer service, administrative and ICT), reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions, and do not repeat anyone already counted in a named division. Feeds the Other Divisions Employees Female %, Other Divisions Employees Total and Total Employees Female KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

name: Other Employees Male
definition: The number of male employees in divisions not covered by the named categories (executive, technical, finance, procurement, human resources, PR/marketing/customer service, administrative and ICT), reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions, and do not repeat anyone already counted in a named division. Feeds the Other Divisions Employees Male %, Other Divisions Employees Total and Total Employees Male KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

name: Other Employees Total
definition: The total number of employees in divisions not covered by the named categories (executive, technical, finance, procurement, human resources, PR/marketing/customer service, administrative and ICT), in employees. It is calculated as the sum of the reported male and female counts for these other divisions, so no separate entry is required. Feeds the Other Divisions Employees Female % and Other Divisions Employees Male % KPIs. If the total looks wrong, correct the underlying male and female counts rather than this value.

name: PR Marketing and Customer Service Employees Female
definition: The number of female employees in the utility's public relations, marketing and customer service division, reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll, including call-centre and front-counter customer service staff; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the PR Marketing and CustService Employees Female %, PR Marketing and CustService Employees Total and Total Employees Female KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

name: PR Marketing and Customer Service Employees Male
definition: The number of male employees in the utility's public relations, marketing and customer service division, reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll, including call-centre and front-counter customer service staff; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the PR Marketing and CustService Employees Male %, PR Marketing and CustService Employees Total and Total Employees Male KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

name: PR Marketing and Customer Service Employees Total
definition: The total number of employees in the utility's public relations, marketing and customer service division, in employees. It is calculated as the sum of the reported male and female counts for this division, so no separate entry is required. Feeds the PR Marketing and CustService Employees Female % and PR Marketing and CustService Employees Male % KPIs. If the total looks wrong, correct the underlying male and female counts rather than this value.

name: Procurement Employees Female
definition: The number of female employees in the utility's procurement division (purchasing and supply chain), reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the Procurement Employees Female %, Procurement Employees Total and Total Employees Female KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

name: Procurement Employees Male
definition: The number of male employees in the utility's procurement division (purchasing and supply chain), reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the Procurement Employees Male %, Procurement Employees Total and Total Employees Male KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

name: Procurement Employees Total
definition: The total number of employees in the utility's procurement division (purchasing and supply chain), in employees. It is calculated as the sum of the reported male and female procurement employee counts, so no separate entry is required. Feeds the Procurement Employees Female % and Procurement Employees Male % KPIs. If the total looks wrong, correct the underlying male and female counts rather than this value.

name: Technical Employees Female
definition: The number of female employees in the utility's technical division (engineering, generation, network operations and similar technical roles), reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll, including apprentices and tradespeople; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the Technical Employees Female %, Technical Employees Total and Total Employees Female KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

name: Technical Employees Male
definition: The number of male employees in the utility's technical division (engineering, generation, network operations and similar technical roles), reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll, including apprentices and tradespeople; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the Technical Employees Male %, Technical Employees Total and Total Employees Male KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

name: Technical Employees Total
definition: The total number of employees in the utility's technical division (engineering, generation, network operations and similar technical roles), in employees. It is calculated as the sum of the reported male and female technical employee counts, so no separate entry is required. Feeds the Technical Employees Female % and Technical Employees Male % KPIs. If the total looks wrong, correct the underlying male and female counts rather than this value.

name: Hours Lost to Work Related Injuries
definition: The total number of scheduled work hours lost during the reporting year because of work-related injuries, in hours. Count hours that the utility's own employees were rostered to work but could not because of a lost-time injury; exclude contractor injuries and absences unrelated to workplace injury. Feeds the Lost Time Injury Duration Rate KPI. Include hours lost during the reporting year even where the injury itself occurred in an earlier year.

name: Number of Work Related Injuries
definition: The number of work-related injury incidents recorded during the reporting year, in incidents. Count injuries to the utility's own employees arising out of or in the course of work that resulted in lost work time; exclude contractor injuries and first-aid-only cases that caused no lost time. Feeds the Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate KPI. Record each qualifying incident once, in the year it occurred.

name: Hours Paid - Distribution
definition: The total number of hours paid to employees in the utility's distribution division during the reporting year, in hours. Include all remunerated hours for employees on the utility's payroll — ordinary time, overtime and paid leave such as annual and sick leave; exclude contractor hours. Feeds the FTE Paid Hours - Distribution and FTE Worked Hours - Distribution KPIs. Paid hours are normally higher than worked hours because they include paid leave and public holidays.

name: Hours Paid - Other Electrical
definition: The total number of hours paid to employees in the utility's other electrical functions — electrical activities outside generation, transmission and distribution — during the reporting year, in hours. Include all remunerated hours for employees on the utility's payroll — ordinary time, overtime and paid leave such as annual and sick leave; exclude contractor hours. Feeds the FTE Paid Hours - Other Electrical KPI. Paid hours are normally higher than worked hours because they include paid leave and public holidays.

name: Hours Paid - Transmission
definition: The total number of hours paid to employees in the utility's transmission division during the reporting year, in hours. Include all remunerated hours for employees on the utility's payroll — ordinary time, overtime and paid leave such as annual and sick leave; exclude contractor hours. Feeds the FTE Paid Hours - Transmission and FTE Worked Hours - Transmission KPIs. Paid hours are normally higher than worked hours because they include paid leave and public holidays.

name: Hours Worked - Distribution
definition: The total number of hours actually worked by employees in the utility's distribution division during the reporting year, in hours. Include ordinary time and overtime actually worked by employees on the utility's payroll; exclude paid leave, public holidays and contractor hours. Feeds the FTE Worked Hours - Distribution KPI and the Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate. Do not report paid hours here — leave and holidays are paid but not worked.

name: Hours Worked - Other Electrical
definition: The total number of hours actually worked by employees in the utility's other electrical functions — electrical activities outside generation, transmission and distribution — during the reporting year, in hours. Include ordinary time and overtime actually worked by employees on the utility's payroll; exclude paid leave, public holidays and contractor hours. Feeds the FTE Worked Hours - Other Electrical KPI and the Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate. Do not report paid hours here — leave and holidays are paid but not worked.

name: Hours Worked - Transmission
definition: The total number of hours actually worked by employees in the utility's transmission division during the reporting year, in hours. Include ordinary time and overtime actually worked by employees on the utility's payroll; exclude paid leave, public holidays and contractor hours. Feeds the FTE Worked Hours - Transmission KPI. Do not report paid hours here — leave and holidays are paid but not worked.

name: Standard Work Hours - Distribution
definition: The standard annual work hours for one full-time employee in the utility's distribution division, in hours. Report the contracted or rostered hours a single full-time employee is expected to work in the year (for example, standard weekly hours multiplied by the number of working weeks), not the division-wide total and not hours actually worked or paid. Feeds the FTE Paid Hours - Distribution and FTE Worked Hours - Distribution KPIs, where it is the divisor that converts total hours into FTEs. A common error is entering the division's total hours instead of the per-employee standard.

name: Standard Work Hours - Other Electrical
definition: The standard annual work hours for one full-time employee in the utility's other electrical functions — electrical activities outside generation, transmission and distribution — in hours. Report the contracted or rostered hours a single full-time employee is expected to work in the year (for example, standard weekly hours multiplied by the number of working weeks), not the function-wide total and not hours actually worked or paid. Feeds the FTE Paid Hours - Other Electrical and FTE Worked Hours - Other Electrical KPIs, where it is the divisor that converts total hours into FTEs. A common error is entering the total hours for the function instead of the per-employee standard.

name: Standard Work Hours - Renewable Generation
definition: The standard annual work hours for one full-time employee in the utility's renewable generation function, in hours. Report the contracted or rostered hours a single full-time employee is expected to work in the year (for example, standard weekly hours multiplied by the number of working weeks), not the function-wide total and not hours actually worked or paid. Feeds the FTE Paid Hours - Renewable Generation and FTE Worked Hours - Renewable Generation KPIs, where it is the divisor that converts total hours into FTEs. A common error is entering the total hours for the function instead of the per-employee standard.

name: Standard Work Hours - Transmission
definition: The standard annual work hours for one full-time employee in the utility's transmission division, in hours. Report the contracted or rostered hours a single full-time employee is expected to work in the year (for example, standard weekly hours multiplied by the number of working weeks), not the division-wide total and not hours actually worked or paid. Feeds the FTE Paid Hours - Transmission and FTE Worked Hours - Transmission KPIs, where it is the divisor that converts total hours into FTEs. A common error is entering the division's total hours instead of the per-employee standard.

name: Distribution Network All Downtime
definition: The total duration of outages on the distribution network during the reporting period, expressed in hours. It is calculated by summing the hours of planned downtime and unplanned (forced) downtime recorded for the distribution network in the service area, so it should reconcile with the separately reported planned and unplanned downtime figures. A common pitfall is entering customer-hours or equipment-hours of interruption instead of hours of network downtime.

name: Distribution Network Length
definition: The total circuit length of the utility's distribution network, in kilometres (km). Include all medium-voltage and low-voltage overhead lines and underground cables owned and operated by the utility in the service area; exclude lines operating at transmission voltage, which are reported separately under Transmission Network Length. This input feeds the Distribution O&M Cost per km and Distribution Reliability KPIs, so an over- or under-stated length distorts cost-per-kilometre and outage-rate comparisons across utilities. A common pitfall is reporting route length rather than circuit length where several circuits share the same poles or trench.

name: Distribution Network Planned Downtime Events
definition: The number of planned outage events on the distribution network during the reporting period, expressed as a count of events. Count only interruptions of distribution plant that were scheduled in advance (for example maintenance, upgrades or new connections) with customers notified beforehand; unplanned (forced) events are reported separately, and momentary interruptions of less than one minute are excluded by standard benchmarking convention. A common pitfall is counting a single planned job that is switched in several stages as multiple separate events.

name: Distribution Network Unplanned Downtime Events
definition: The number of unplanned (forced) outage events on the distribution network during the reporting period, expressed as a count of events. Include only interruptions of distribution plant caused by faults, equipment failure, weather or third-party damage without advance notice; planned events are reported separately, and momentary interruptions of less than one minute are excluded by standard benchmarking convention. This input feeds the Distribution Reliability KPI, so consistent event counting is essential for year-on-year and cross-utility comparison. A common pitfall is including outages that originated in generation or transmission rather than in the distribution network itself.

name: Distribution Transformer Capacity
definition: The total installed capacity of distribution transformers in the service area, expressed in megavolt-amperes (MVA). Sum the nameplate ratings of all distribution (MV/LV) transformers in service, including pole-mounted, pad-mounted and ground-mounted units; exclude transmission grid or power-station transformers. This input feeds the Transformer Utilization Factor KPI, which compares peak demand against installed transformer capacity. A common pitfall is entering values in kVA instead of MVA — divide kVA nameplate totals by 1,000.

name: Electricity Demand Average Load
definition: The average load on the power system over the reporting period, expressed in MWh per hour of the period (numerically equal to the average demand in MW). It should be derived as the total electricity delivered to the network (net, sent out) divided by the number of hours in the period, measured on the same basis as the peak load figure. This input feeds the Load Factor KPI, which compares average load with peak load to show how evenly the system is utilised. A common pitfall is entering the total annual energy in MWh rather than the hourly average, which inflates the value by several thousand times.

name: Electricity Demand Peak Load
definition: The maximum load on the power system during the reporting period, expressed in MWh for the peak hour (numerically equal to the peak demand in MW when measured over a one-hour interval). Report the highest coincident system peak for the service area measured at the sent-out (net) level, after station auxiliaries, rather than the sum of individual feeder or station peaks, which overstates the true system maximum. This input feeds the Load Factor KPI, so it must be measured on the same basis as the average load figure. A common pitfall is reporting an instantaneous peak in kW or MW, or a gross generation peak, instead of the net hourly system peak.

name: Electricity Sold to Customers
definition: The total electricity billed to customers during the reporting period, expressed in MWh. Include all metered sales to residential, commercial, industrial and government customers in the service area, plus street lighting where it is billed; exclude the utility's own internal consumption and any unbilled or unmetered supply, which are captured as losses. This input feeds the Customer Consumption, Network Delivery Losses and Transmission Network Losses KPIs, so under-recorded sales directly overstate reported network losses. A common pitfall is entering values in kWh rather than MWh — divide kWh billing totals by 1,000.

name: Hours in Period
definition: The total number of hours in the reporting period, expressed in hours. For a full reporting year this is 8,760 hours (8,784 in a leap year); if data covers a shorter or different period, enter the actual number of hours in that period. This input feeds the Generator Availability Factor, Generator Forced Outage Indicator and Generator Planned Outage Indicator KPIs, which express generator outage and available hours as a share of total period hours. A common pitfall is misalignment between this figure and the period covered by the generation and outage data — all must relate to the same fiscal or calendar year.

name: Total Interruptions Customers Affected
definition: The total number of customer interruptions from all supply interruptions during the reporting period, expressed as a count of customers. It is calculated by adding the customers affected by planned interruptions to the customers affected by unplanned (forced) interruptions, counting a customer once for every event that interrupts them rather than as unique customers. Momentary interruptions of less than one minute are excluded, consistent with the planned and unplanned inputs from which it is built. A common pitfall is expecting this to equal the number of distinct customers interrupted — it is a sum of customer-interruptions and can exceed the total customer base.

name: Total Interruptions Events
definition: The total number of supply interruption events from all causes during the reporting period, expressed as a count of events. It is calculated by adding the number of planned interruption events to the number of unplanned (forced) interruption events. Momentary interruptions of less than one minute are excluded, consistent with the planned and unplanned inputs from which it is built. A common pitfall is any mismatch with the separately reported planned and unplanned event counts — the three figures must reconcile.

name: Total Planned Interruptions Customers Affected
definition: The total number of customers affected by planned supply interruptions during the reporting period, expressed as a count of customers. For each planned event (scheduled in advance with customers notified), count the customers whose supply was interrupted and sum across all events — a customer interrupted by three planned events counts three times; momentary interruptions of less than one minute are excluded by standard benchmarking convention. This input feeds the Planned SAIDI and Planned SAIFI KPIs, so accurate customer counts per event directly determine the utility's published reliability indices. A common pitfall is reporting unique customers rather than customer-interruptions, which understates the reliability indices.

name: Total Planned Interruptions Events
definition: The number of planned supply interruption events during the reporting period, expressed as a count of events. Count only interruptions that were scheduled in advance (for example for maintenance, network upgrades or new connections) with prior notice to customers; unplanned (forced) interruptions are reported separately, and momentary interruptions of less than one minute are excluded by standard benchmarking convention. This input feeds the Planned SAIFI KPI, so consistent event definitions are essential for comparability. A common pitfall is counting each switching stage of a single planned job as a separate event.

name: Total Unplanned Interruptions Customers Affected
definition: The total number of customers affected by unplanned (forced) supply interruptions during the reporting period, expressed as a count of customers. For each unplanned event — faults, equipment failure, weather, vegetation or third-party damage occurring without advance notice — count the customers whose supply was interrupted and sum across all events, counting a customer once per event; momentary interruptions of less than one minute are excluded by standard benchmarking convention. A common pitfall is reporting unique customers rather than customer-interruptions, or omitting events restored quickly by automatic reclosing that still lasted one minute or longer.

name: Total Unplanned Interruptions Events
definition: The number of unplanned (forced) supply interruption events during the reporting period, expressed as a count of events. Include only interruptions occurring without advance notice — faults, equipment failure, weather, vegetation or third-party damage; planned interruptions are reported separately, and momentary interruptions of less than one minute are excluded by standard benchmarking convention. A common pitfall is inconsistent treatment of a single fault with staged restoration — it should normally be counted as one event, not one per restoration step.

name: Transmission Electricity Sold to Customers
definition: The electricity sold to customers supplied directly from the transmission network during the reporting period, expressed in MWh. Include only metered sales to customers connected at transmission voltage (typically large industrial or bulk-supply customers taking supply before the distribution network); sales delivered through the distribution network are captured under Electricity Sold to Customers. This input feeds the Transmission Network Losses KPI, allowing transmission losses to be separated from distribution losses. A common pitfall is double-counting these sales in both this input and the general electricity-sold figure, which understates reported losses.

name: Transmission Network All Downtime Events
definition: The total number of outage events on the transmission network during the reporting period, expressed as a count of events. It is calculated by adding planned (scheduled) downtime events to unplanned (forced) downtime events recorded for the transmission network in the service area, so it should reconcile with the separately reported planned and unplanned figures. Utilities without a distinct transmission system (no network operating at transmission voltage) do not report this input. A common pitfall is including distribution-level outages in the transmission count.

name: Transmission Network Customers Served
definition: The number of customers supplied directly from the transmission network, expressed as a count of customers. Count metered customer connection points at transmission voltage (typically large industrial or bulk-supply customers), not the wider population served downstream through the distribution network; utilities without a distinct transmission system do not report this input. A common pitfall is reporting the total customer base instead of only the transmission-connected customers, which for most Pacific utilities is a very small number.

name: Transmission Network Length
definition: The total circuit length of the utility's transmission network, in kilometres (km). Include all overhead lines and underground cables operating at transmission voltage that the utility owns and operates; distribution-voltage lines are reported separately under Distribution Network Length, and utilities with no distinct transmission system do not report this input. This input feeds the Transmission Reliability KPI, which normalises transmission outages by network length. A common pitfall is reporting route length rather than circuit length where double-circuit towers carry more than one circuit.

name: Transmission Network Planned Downtime
definition: The total duration of planned outages on the transmission network during the reporting period, expressed in hours. Include only downtime that was scheduled in advance (for example for maintenance, inspections or construction); unplanned (forced) downtime is reported separately, and utilities without a distinct transmission system do not report this input. A common pitfall is reporting the elapsed duration of the whole work programme rather than the actual hours the transmission plant was out of service.
